name: Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia
sources_2026_10_04: Race story and incident causes from the Formula 1 race report (2026-10-04), the FIA race report (2026-10-04) and Autosport's full race report (2026-10-04). Classification, qualifying, starting grid and fastest laps verified against the FIA final race classification, final qualifying classification and final starting grid, plus the official Formula 1 result tables. Penalties checked against FIA stewards' documents 17, 18, 19, 52, 58 and 59; the five-place Colapinto collision penalty is identified on the FIA final-grid document as Azerbaijan stewards' document 66. Where Autosport's results table labels Albon's retirement an accident, the FIA race report's dated gearbox-failure account is preferred. Data notes: Bottas's classified distance is 7 laps on the FIA sheet while the BBC report places his Turn 13 spin on lap nine; the lap-nine figure is the sourced incident lap, not a classified-distance claim.
summary: Max Verstappen converted pole into his first win of 2026, beating Kimi Antonelli by 2.307s while Lewis Hamilton completed Ferrari's recovery in third. Heavy rain delayed the start and forced a suspended start procedure; Bottas's lap-nine spin triggered the first Safety Car, while Albon's gearbox failure caused the late Virtual Safety Car and Safety Car sequence. Hamilton and Leclerc recovered from their slick-tyre gamble to finish third and fourth, while Hadjar fell from P8 on the grid to fifth and Lindblad recovered from the back row to score the final point. Russell retired from a certain podium place with a power-unit failure after 49 laps, and Bortoleto's 10-second collision penalty left him 18th. This was Red Bull Ford Powertrains' maiden win and F1's first race at Sepang since 2017.

classification.stewardNote: Won by 2.307s. Converted pole after losing the start to both Mercedes, reclaimed the lead at the first restart, and controlled the late Safety Car restart.
+2.307s. Swept into the lead at the start, regained second from Russell on lap 21, and extended his championship lead after Russell retired.
+4.919s. Started on slicks and fell deep into the order, then recovered through the field to pass Hadjar for third on lap 53.
Started P8 after a five-place grid penalty for an extra power-unit element and recovered to fifth; both Ferraris passed him in the closing laps.
Received a reprimand for driving erratically under Safety Car conditions after avoiding the slowing cars ahead and running through the gravel.
Started P22 after a 30-place grid penalty for extra power-unit elements and recovered to P10 for the final point.
Audi was fined 30,000 euro, with 20,000 euro suspended for 12 months, after an unsafe pit-stop release involving his car.
Started P21 after 15 grid-penalty places: five for causing the Baku collision and 10 for an extra power-unit element; finished P13.
Dropped from P9 to P16 as his slick-tyre gamble struggled in the wet-to-dry crossover.
Spun to P18 after Bortoleto's Turn 2 contact; moved to P17 after Bortoleto's 10-second penalty. Williams was also fined 100 euro for reconnaissance-lap pit-lane speeding.
Received a 10-second penalty for causing a Turn 2 collision with Sainz, dropping from P17 to P18.
Technical. Retired on the start/finish straight with a power-unit failure after 49 laps, classified P20 from P7 on the grid.
Technical. Stopped with a gearbox issue on lap 41, bringing out the Virtual Safety Car and then the Safety Car.
